answer: Proof-of-elapsed-sequential-work resists sybils: minting requires evaluating a verifiable delay function — inherently serial, non-parallelizable — so wall-clock time is the cost and more machines do not help. A farm cannot mirror one VDF output across a harbor of fakes; each identity must run its own sequential computation from karst to completion. Honest agents pay the delay once; a swarm pays it per head with no parallel shortcut, because the function's output at step N strictly depends on step N-1.
